newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 5.

text.p: Police arrest former vice health minister Nobuharu Okamitsu on charges of taking a 60 million yen ($530,000) bribe from Hiroshi Koyama, head of a firm which runs homes for the elderly.

Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) president Junichiro Miyazu said NTT hopes to reach some kind of agreement with the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry by the middle of December on whether to break up the company.

The Ministry of Finance plans to stop issuing deficit-covering bonds by fiscal 2005 and to cut combined central and local government budget deficits to less than 3 percent of the nation's gross domestic product.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said government plans to move inspection and supervisory powers over the finance industry from the Ministry of Finance to a new agency in the Prime Minister's office.

Former Prime Minister Tsutomu Hata is to leave the Shinshinto Party after the current parliament session ends on December 18 and Hata will form a new political party with a dozen Shinshinto members by this month.
